vision_features.image_context: Close-up of a soybean plant in a field setting. Visible organs include green stems, and multiple seed pods attached at nodes along the stems. The surrounding field shows extensively dried, brown, straw-like vegetation and dark soil at the base.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Pods: The pods throughout the plant are tan to light brown in color, elongated oval shape (approximately 30–40 mm long, 8–10 mm wide), appearing flat and papery with very little or no seed fill visible — they appear thin and shrunken rather than plump. The pod surfaces are dry and slightly wrinkled. Fine short hairs (whitish, ~1 mm) are visible on pod surfaces. Distribution: pods present at multiple nodes along the entire visible stem length, uniformly underdeveloped.
2. Pods at mid and lower nodes: Several pods appear noticeably flattened and nearly empty, with a slightly darker tan-brown coloration compared to normally filled pods. A few small dark specks (pinpoint size, black) are visible at node attachment points near mid-stem.
3. Stems: The main stems remain green and appear relatively healthy and upright, with fine short hairs visible. No obvious discoloration or structural damage to the stems themselves.
4. Surrounding foliage: All leaves on this plant and surrounding plants have completely dried and dropped or shriveled to a brown papery state, leaving bare stems — consistent with very late-season or stress-related early leaf drop. Leaf debris visible at the soil level is dark brown and desiccated.
vision_features.absences:
1. No plump, fully filled pods visible — none of the pods show the rounded, bulging profile expected of well-developed seeds inside.
2. No green leaf tissue remaining on the plant — all leaves have senesced or abscised.
3. No powdery, slimy, or fuzzy surface coating on the pods or stems beyond the normal fine hair coverage.
4. No large dark brown or sunken marks/patches on the pod walls that would suggest localized damage to individual pod surfaces.
vision_features.summary: The plant is a soybean at late reproductive/near-maturity stage with green stems but completely defoliated, bearing multiple pods at several nodes along the stems. The most striking feature is that nearly all pods appear flat, thin, and largely empty of seed fill, with a uniform tan-brown dry color and papery texture. The surrounding field vegetation is entirely dried and brown, suggesting late-season conditions or significant stress. The single most unusual visual feature is the uniformly underfilled, flat and shrunken appearance of the pods across all nodes, contrasting with the still-green stems.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. ────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Septoria brown spot, Bacterial pustule, Downy mildew, Soybean rust, Soybean vein necrosis, Insect and mite Injury
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Green_stem_disorder' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Presence of linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on stems
Green_stem_disorder: No description is available for Green Stem Disorder, so no specific visual markers can be cited from the knowledge base.
Diaporthe: Diaporthe shows either sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish-brown margins near lower nodes (stem canker) or characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems (pod and stem blight), with possible thin black 'zone lines' inside lower stems.
Decision rule  : IF the stem displays linear rows of black specks and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, THEN classify as Diaporthe; if neither feature is present and no description matches, Green Stem Disorder cannot be visually confirmed from available knowledge-base data.
